title: do...while Loops: Execute at Least Once
learningObjectives: Describe how do...while executes its body before checking its condition.
Trace a do...while loop to predict output and iterations.
Prevent endless repetition by changing loop state and choosing a clear stopping condition.

understand.concept: A do...while loop executes its body first and checks the condition afterward. If the condition is true, it repeats; if false, it stops. Since the check occurs after the first run, the body always executes at least once—even if the condition is false initially.
understand.whyItMatters: Some tasks need an initial action before deciding whether to repeat, such as showing a menu, attempting a task, or asking for input before deciding whether another attempt is needed.
understand.analogy: Try a key in a lock once, then ask, 'Should I try again?' The first attempt happens before the repeat decision.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy focuses on action-before-check. A program still needs a reliable condition and a state change to avoid endless repetition.

explain.narrative: A do...while loop starts with do and a statement block, followed by while and a condition. The body runs first; then the condition is evaluated. True returns execution to the body, while false continues after the loop. In JavaScript, a semicolon follows the condition. Use this structure when one initial execution is required, and update the state that controls repetition.

commonMistakes: Expecting do...while to skip the body when its condition is initially false.
Forgetting the semicolon after the condition.
Updating a variable that the condition does not use.
Miscounting because the condition is checked after the body.
Choosing do...while when zero iterations are allowed and preferable.

guidedTask.title: Guided: Display a greeting at least once
guidedTask.instructions: Print Welcome! at least once, then repeat while a counter is less than 3. Update the counter so the loop ends.
steps: Initialize a counter before the loop.
Print Welcome! inside the do body.
Increment the counter in the body.
Put the while condition after the closing brace.
Include the ending semicolon and trace the output.

independentTask.title: Independent: Collect at least one attempt
independentTask.instructions: Print Try task on each attempt. Start attempts at 0 and repeat using do...while until attempts reaches 4. Print Finished after the loop.
requirements: Use do...while so the body precedes the condition check.
Print the task message inside the body.
Explain why the body runs at least once even if the initial condition is false.

questions.prompt: What is the defining behavior of a do...while loop?
options: It executes its body before checking the condition
questions.answer: It executes its body before checking the condition
questions.explanation: The first iteration happens before the condition is evaluated.

questions.prompt: If the condition is false initially, how many times does a do...while body run?
questions.explanation: The body runs before the initial condition check.

questions.prompt: What punctuation follows the while(condition) in JavaScript do...while syntax?
questions.explanation: The statement ends with a semicolon.

questions.prompt: What can cause a do...while loop to never end?
options: The condition remains true because the relevant state never changes
The condition is checked after the body
questions.answer: The condition remains true because the relevant state never changes
questions.explanation: If no progress makes the condition false, the loop can continue indefinitely.

questions.prompt: When is do...while a good choice?
options: When the body must run at least once before deciding to repeat
When the body must never run
questions.answer: When the body must run at least once before deciding to repeat
questions.explanation: Post-test behavior guarantees one initial execution.
